title.zh: 卷七十六 列傳第三十六 朱脩之 宗愨 王玄謨
title.en: Volume 76 Biographies 36: Zhu Xiuzhi, Zong Que, Wang Xuanmo
title.raw: 卷七十六 列傳第三十六 朱脩之 宗愨 王玄謨 Volume 76 Biographies 36: Zhu Xiuzhi, Zong Que, Wang Xuanmo

sentences.zh: 朱脩之

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi

sentences.zh: 朱脩之字恭祖，義陽平氏人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi, style name Gongzu, was a man of Pingshi in Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi, whose courtesy name was Gongzu, came from Pingshi in Yiyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖燾，晉平西將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tao was Grand General Who Pacifies the West under the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tao had held the Jin post of Grand General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 祖序，豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xu was Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xu had served as Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父諶，益州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Chen was Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chen had served as Inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 脩之自州主簿遷司徒從事中郎，文帝謂曰：「卿曾祖昔為王導丞相中郎，卿今又為王弘中郎，可謂不忝爾祖矣。」

translations.literal: Xiuzhi rose from provincial chief clerk to Attendant Gentleman of the Minister over the Masses. Emperor Wen said to him, "Your great-grandfather once served as Director under Chancellor Wang Dao, and you now serve as Director under Wang Hong—you truly do not disgrace your ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi advanced from provincial chief clerk to Attendant Gentleman under the Minister over the Masses (Situ). Emperor Wen told him, "Your great-grandfather once served as a director in Chancellor Wang Dao's secretariat, and you now hold the same post under Wang Hong—you have not disgraced your forebears."

sentences.zh: 後隨到彥之北伐。

translations.literal: Later he followed Dao Yanzhi on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He later accompanied Dao Yanzhi on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 彥之自河南回，留脩之戍滑臺，為虜所圍，數月糧盡，將士熏鼠食之，遂陷於虜。

translations.literal: When Yanzhi withdrew from south of the Yellow River, he left Xiuzhi to garrison Huatai. The barbarians besieged it; after months the grain was exhausted and the officers and men smoked out rats to eat them, and at last the place fell to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhi pulled back from the region south of the Yellow River, he left Xiuzhi to hold Huatai. The enemy surrounded the city; after several months the stores were gone and the troops smoked out rats for food, until the fortress finally fell.

sentences.zh: 初，脩之母聞其被圍既久，常憂之，忽一旦乳汁驚出，母號泣告家人曰：「吾今已老，忽復有乳汁，斯不祥矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiuzhi's mother heard that he had been besieged for so long, she had been constantly anxious. Suddenly one day her milk came out in a start; weeping, she told the household, "I am old now, yet milk has come again—this is an ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiuzhi's mother had worried constantly after hearing he had been under siege so long. Then one day her milk suddenly flowed again. Weeping, she told the family, "I am already old, yet milk has returned—this cannot be auspicious.

sentences.zh: 吾兒其不利乎。」

translations.literal: Will it not go ill with my son?"
translations.idiomatic: Surely some misfortune awaits my son?"

sentences.zh: 後問至，脩之果以此日陷沒。

translations.literal: When word later arrived, Xiuzhi had indeed fallen on that very day.
translations.idiomatic: When news finally came, Xiuzhi had indeed been lost on that same day.

sentences.zh: 託跋燾嘉其守節，以為侍中，妻以宗室女。

translations.literal: Tuoba Tao admired his steadfastness, made him Palace Attendant, and gave him an imperial-clan woman in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Tao admired his constancy, appointed him Palace Attendant, and married him to a woman of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 脩之潛謀南歸，妻疑之，每流涕問其意，脩之深嘉其義，竟不告也。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi secretly plotted to return south. His wife suspected this and, weeping, repeatedly asked his intent; Xiuzhi deeply admired her loyalty yet never told her.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi secretly planned to flee south. His wife grew suspicious and, in tears, kept asking what he intended; he admired her devotion deeply but never confided in her.

sentences.zh: 後鮮卑馮弘稱燕王，治黃龍城，託跋燾伐之，脩之與同沒人邢懷明並從。

translations.literal: Later the Xianbei Feng Hong styled himself King of Yan and ruled from Huanglongcheng. Tuoba Tao attacked him, and Xiuzhi went along with fellow captive Xing Huaiming.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Xianbei Feng Hong declared himself King of Yan and ruled from Huanglongcheng. When Tuoba Tao marched against him, Xiuzhi followed with fellow captive Xing Huaiming.

sentences.zh: 又有徐卓者，復欲率南人竊發，事泄被誅。

translations.literal: There was also Xu Zhuo, who again wished to lead southerners in a secret rising; the plot leaked and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Another captive, Xu Zhuo, tried to rally the southerners in a covert uprising; the plot was exposed and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 脩之、懷明懼奔馮弘，弘不禮。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi and Huaiming, in fear, fled to Feng Hong, who did not treat them with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for their lives, Xiuzhi and Huaiming fled to Feng Hong, who showed them no honor.

sentences.zh: 留一年，會宋使傳詔至，脩之名位素顯，傳詔見即拜之，彼國敬傳詔，謂為「天子邊人」，見其致敬於脩之，乃始加禮。

translations.literal: They remained a year. Then a Song envoy bearing an imperial edict arrived. Xiuzhi's name and rank were well known, and the edict-bearer bowed to him at once. That state revered the edict-bearer, calling him "the Son of Heaven's man from the border," and when they saw him pay homage to Xiuzhi they at last treated Xiuzhi with respect.
translations.idiomatic: They stayed a year. Then a Song envoy arrived bearing an imperial message. Xiuzhi's standing was already well known, and the bearer of the message bowed to him immediately. The northerners revered the envoy as "the Son of Heaven's man from the frontier"; seeing him defer to Xiuzhi, they finally treated Xiuzhi with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 時魏屢伐弘，或說弘遣脩之歸求救，遂遣之。

translations.literal: At that time Wei repeatedly attacked Hong. Some urged Hong to send Xiuzhi back to seek Song aid, and he sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was then attacking Hong repeatedly. Some advised Hong to send Xiuzhi south to beg Song for rescue, and Hong dispatched him.

sentences.zh: 泛海至東萊，遇猛風柁折，垂以長索，船乃復正。

translations.literal: He crossed the sea to Donglai. A fierce wind broke the rudder; they lowered a long rope and the vessel righted itself.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed the sea to Donglai. A violent gale snapped the rudder; they hung a long rope over the side and the ship steadied again.

sentences.zh: 海師望見飛鳥，知其近岸，須臾至東萊。

translations.literal: The pilot, seeing birds in flight, knew land was near; in a moment they reached Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: The pilot sighted birds overhead, knew shore was near, and within moments they made Donglai.

sentences.zh: 元嘉九年，至京邑，以為黃門侍郎，累遷江夏內史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia he reached the capital and was made Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then was promoted repeatedly to Interior Minister of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia he reached the capital, was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, and rose step by step to Interior Minister of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史劉道產卒，羣蠻大動，脩之為征西司馬討蠻，失利。

translations.literal: When Inspector of Yongzhou Liu Daochan died, the tribal peoples rose in great numbers. Xiuzhi served as Western Campaigning Marshal and attacked the tribes but was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Daochan, Inspector of Yongzhou, died, the tribal peoples stirred on a large scale. Xiuzhi served as Western Campaigning Marshal against them but met defeat.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，為寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was made Colonel Pacifying the Tribes and Inspector of Yongzhou, with overall command added.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was made Colonel Pacifying the Tribes and Inspector of Yongzhou, with overall military authority.

sentences.zh: 脩之在政寬簡，士眾悅附。

translations.literal: In his administration Xiuzhi was lenient and simple; officers and men were glad to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was easy and unassuming; soldiers and officials gladly attached themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 及荊州刺史南郡王義宣反，檄脩之舉兵，脩之偽與之同，而遣使陳誠於帝。

translations.literal: When the Inspector of Jingzhou, the Prince of Nanjun Yixuan, rebelled, he summoned Xiuzhi to raise troops. Xiuzhi pretended to agree while sending an envoy to declare his loyalty to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan, Prince of Nanjun and Inspector of Jingzhou, rebelled, he called on Xiuzhi to join the revolt. Xiuzhi feigned agreement while sending an envoy to pledge his loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，以為荊州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and made him Inspector of Jingzhou with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and appointed him Inspector of Jingzhou with overall military authority.

sentences.zh: 義宣聞脩之不與己同，乃以魯秀為雍州刺史，擊襄陽。

translations.literal: When Yixuan learned that Xiuzhi would not join him, he appointed Lu Xiu Inspector of Yongzhou and attacked Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Xiuzhi would not stand with him, Yixuan named Lu Xiu Inspector of Yongzhou and marched on Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 脩之命斷馬鞍山道，秀不得前，乃退。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi ordered the Ma'an Mountain road cut; Xiu could not advance and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi had the Ma'an Mountain route blocked; Xiu could not get through and retreated.

sentences.zh: 及義宣敗於梁山，單舟南走，脩之率眾南定遺寇。

translations.literal: When Yixuan was defeated at Liangshan and fled south in a lone boat, Xiuzhi led his forces south to pacify the remnant bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After Yixuan was beaten at Liangshan and fled south alone by boat, Xiuzhi led his troops south to subdue the scattered rebels.

sentences.zh: 時竺超民執義宣，脩之至，乃殺之，以功封南昌縣侯。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Chaomin held Yixuan prisoner. When Xiuzhi arrived he killed Yixuan and, for his merit, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Chaomin then held Yixuan captive. Xiuzhi arrived, killed Yixuan, and for this service was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanchang county.

sentences.zh: 脩之治身清約，凡所贈貺，一無所受，有餉，或受之，而旋與佐吏賭之，終不入己，唯以撫納羣蠻為務。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi conducted himself with frugal integrity. He accepted none of the gifts offered him. If something was sent, he might take it but at once wager it with his staff officers, never keeping it for himself; his sole concern was to win over the tribal peoples.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly and with integrity, refusing every gift that came to him. On the rare occasion he accepted a present, he immediately staked it in wagers with his aides and never kept it; his one aim was to conciliate the tribal peoples.

sentences.zh: 徵為左民尚書，轉領軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Minister of the Left for the People and then transferred to General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as Minister of the Left for the People, then promoted to General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 去鎮，秋毫不犯，計在州然油及牛馬穀草，以私錢十六萬償之。

translations.literal: On leaving his post he took not the slightest thing. He calculated the lamp oil and fodder for cattle and horses consumed in the province and repaid it with 160,000 in private funds.
translations.idiomatic: When he left his command he took nothing whatsoever. He reckoned the lamp oil and fodder for cattle and horses used in the province and reimbursed the treasury with 160,000 cash from his own purse.

sentences.zh: 然性儉剋少恩情，姊在鄉里，飢寒不立，脩之未嘗供贍。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was frugal and stern and showed little familial feeling. His elder sister lived in the countryside in hunger and cold, unable to support herself, yet Xiuzhi never once provided for her.
translations.idiomatic: By nature, however, he was tight-fisted and sparing of affection. His elder sister lived in the countryside in want, yet he never once helped her.

sentences.zh: 嘗往視姊，姊欲激之，為設菜羹粗飯，脩之曰：「此乃貧家好食。」

translations.literal: Once he went to visit her. She wished to stir him and set out vegetable broth and coarse rice. Xiuzhi said, "This is the fine fare of a poor household."
translations.idiomatic: Once he visited her. Hoping to shame him, she served only vegetable broth and coarse grain. Xiuzhi said, "This is exactly the sort of meal a poor family does best."

sentences.zh: 致飽而去。

translations.literal: He ate his fill and left.
translations.idiomatic: He ate until he was full and departed.

sentences.zh: 先是，新野庾彥達為益州刺史，攜姊之鎮，分祿秩之半以供贍之，西土稱焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu Yanda of Xinye had been Inspector of Yizhou. He took his sister to his post and gave her half his salary for her support; the western lands praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yu Yanda of Xinye had served as Inspector of Yizhou, brought his sister to his command, and allotted half his stipend for her upkeep—the western provinces had held this up as a model.

sentences.zh: 脩之後墜車折脚，辭尚書，領崇憲太僕，仍加特進、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later Xiuzhi fell from a carriage and broke his leg. He resigned as Minister but headed the Chongxian Grand Steward of the Palace Studs, and was further given the extraordinary promotion and the golden seal and purple ribbon of the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fell from a carriage and broke his leg. He resigned his ministerial post but retained the title of Grand Steward of the Chongxian Palace Studs, and was further granted extraordinary promotion and the golden seal and purple ribbon of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 以脚疾不堪獨行，特給扶侍。

translations.literal: Because his leg ailment kept him from walking alone, he was specially given attendants to support him.
translations.idiomatic: His injured leg kept him from walking unaided, so he was specially provided with attendants to lean on.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中，特進如故。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, with extraordinary promotion as before.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Palace Attendant, retaining his extraordinary promotion.

sentences.zh: 諡貞侯。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhen ("Steadfast").

sentences.zh: 宗慤

translations.literal: Zong Que
translations.idiomatic: Zong Que

sentences.zh: 宗慤字元幹，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Zong Que, style name Yuangan, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Que, whose courtesy name was Yuangan, came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 叔父炳，高尚不仕。

translations.literal: His uncle Bing was lofty in character and would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Bing was a man of lofty principle who refused public office.

sentences.zh: 慤年少時，炳問其志，慤曰：「願乘長風破萬里浪。」

translations.literal: When Que was young, Bing asked his ambition. Que said, "I wish to ride the long wind and break ten thousand li of waves."
translations.idiomatic: When Que was still young, Bing asked what he hoped to achieve. Que answered, "I mean to ride the long wind and shatter waves ten thousand li away."

sentences.zh: 炳曰：「汝不富貴，即破我家矣。」

translations.literal: Bing said, "If you are not ennobled and wealthy, you will ruin our house."
translations.idiomatic: Bing replied, "Unless you win rank and riches, you will ruin our household."

sentences.zh: 兄泌娶妻，始入門，夜被劫，慤年十四，挺身拒賊，賊十餘人皆披散，不得入室。

translations.literal: When Que's elder brother Mi married, on the very night the bride entered the gate the house was robbed. Que was fourteen and threw himself against the bandits; more than ten of them scattered and could not enter the room.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Mi took a wife and she first crossed the threshold, robbers struck that night. Que was fourteen, charged the thieves alone, and drove more than ten of them off so they could not enter.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，士人並以文義為業，炳素高節，諸子羣從皆好學，而慤獨任氣好武，故不為鄉曲所稱。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was at peace and gentlemen all took literary studies as their calling. Bing was by nature high-minded, and his sons and cousins all loved learning, yet Que alone trusted in force and loved martial affairs, so the neighborhood did not speak well of him.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was then at peace and men of standing devoted themselves to letters. Bing and his kin were all devoted to study, but Que alone relied on brute courage and loved arms, and won no praise in his home district.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭為征北將軍、南兗州刺史，慤隨鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, was General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou; Que followed him to garrison Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, served as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, Que accompanied him to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 時從兄綺為征北府主簿，綺嘗入直，而給吏牛泰與綺妾私通，慤殺泰，綺壯其意，不責也。

translations.literal: At that time Que's cousin Qi was chief clerk of the Pacifying-North headquarters. Once Qi entered duty, but his clerk Niu Tai had an affair with Qi's concubine. Que killed Tai; Qi admired his spirit and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Qi then served as chief clerk on the Pacifying-North staff. Once, while Qi was on duty, a clerk named Niu Tai was carrying on with Qi's concubine. Que killed him; Qi respected his boldness and did not reproach him.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年，伐林邑，慤自奮請行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia they attacked Lin Yi. Que volunteered eagerly for the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia the court attacked Lin Yi. Que boldly volunteered for the expedition.

sentences.zh: 義恭舉慤有膽勇，乃除振武將軍，為安西參軍蕭景憲軍副，隨交州刺史檀和之圍區粟城。

translations.literal: Yigong cited Que's courage and made him General Who Quells the Martial, deputy to the Western Pacification staff officer Xiao Jingxian, following the Inspector of Jiaozhou Tan Hezhi in besieging Qu Su.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong praised his daring and appointed him General Who Quells the Martial, second to Xiao Jingxian on the Western Pacification staff, as they followed Jiaozhou Inspector Tan Hezhi in the siege of Qu Su.

sentences.zh: 林邑遣將范毗沙達來救區粟，和之遣偏軍拒之，為賊所敗。

translations.literal: Lin Yi sent the general Fan Bisha to relieve Qu Su. Hezhi sent a detached force to meet him and was defeated by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi sent General Fan Bisha to relieve Qu Su. Hezhi dispatched a separate column to block him and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 又遣慤，慤乃分軍為數道，偃旗潛進，討破之，拔區粟，入象浦。

translations.literal: He sent Que again. Que divided his army into several columns, lowered their banners, and advanced in secret, defeating the enemy, taking Qu Su, and entering Xiang Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi sent Que out again. Que split his force into several routes, hid their banners, and stole forward, routing the enemy, capturing Qu Su, and pushing on to Xiang Pu.

sentences.zh: 林邑王范陽邁傾國來拒，以具裝被象，前後無際，士卒不能當。

translations.literal: The king of Lin Yi, Fan Yangmai, mustered the whole state to resist. He armored elephants and deployed them in ranks without end; the soldiers could not withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yi's king, Fan Yangmai, mobilized the entire kingdom to resist. He fitted elephants with armor and drew them up in endless lines; the troops could not stand against them.

sentences.zh: 慤曰：「吾聞師子威服百獸。」

translations.literal: Que said, "I have heard that the lion makes all beasts submit."
translations.idiomatic: Que said, "They say the lion makes every beast tremble."

sentences.zh: 乃製其形，與象相禦，象果驚奔，眾因潰散，遂克林邑。

translations.literal: He fashioned its likeness to confront the elephants; the elephants indeed panicked and fled, and the host collapsed. They then took Lin Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He had its likeness made to face the elephants; the beasts panicked and bolted, the army broke, and Lin Yi fell.

sentences.zh: 收其異寶雜物，不可勝計。

translations.literal: They gathered rare treasures and sundry goods beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: They seized exotic treasures and goods beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: 慤一無所取，衣櫛蕭然。

translations.literal: Que took not a single thing; his clothes and toilet articles were bare.
translations.idiomatic: Que took nothing for himself; his wardrobe and kit were as spare as when he had set out.

sentences.zh: 文帝甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen greatly commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 後為隨郡太守，雍州蠻屢為寇，建威將軍沈慶之率慤及柳元景等諸將，分道攻之，羣蠻大潰。

translations.literal: Later he was made Administrator of Suixian. The tribes of Yongzhou raided repeatedly. General Who Establishes Martial Might Shen Qingzhi led Que, Liu Yuanying, and other generals in separate columns to attack them, and the tribes were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Administrator of Suixian. Tribal forces in Yongzhou raided again and again. Shen Qingzhi, General Who Establishes Martial Might, led Que, Liu Yuanying, and others in divided attacks, and the tribes were smashed.

sentences.zh: 又南新郡蠻帥田彥生率部曲反叛，焚燒郡城，屯據白楊山，元景攻之未能下，慤率其所領先登，眾軍隨之，羣蠻由是畏服。

translations.literal: The tribal chief Tian Yansheng of Nanxin also rebelled with his followers, burned the commandery city, and held White Poplar Mountain. Yuanying attacked but could not take it. Que led his own men in the first ascent; the other armies followed, and from then on the tribes feared him.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanxin, the tribal leader Tian Yansheng rose with his bands, burned the commandery seat, and occupied White Poplar Mountain. Yuanying besieged him without success. Que led his own men up first; the rest of the army followed, and the tribes thereafter held him in awe.

sentences.zh: 三十年，孝武伐元凶，以慤為南中郎諮議參軍，領中兵。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, when Emperor Xiaowu attacked the deposed heir Yuanxiong, Que was made advising staff officer of the Southern Palace Attendant and commanded the central guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, when Emperor Xiaowu marched against the deposed heir Yuanxiong, Que served as advising officer on the Southern General of the Household's staff and commanded the central troops.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，以為左衞將軍，封洮陽侯，功次柳元景。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Que was made General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Taoyang, his merit ranking just after Liu Yuanying's.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaowu's accession, Que was made General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Marquis of Taoyang; his merit stood just below Liu Yuanying's.

sentences.zh: 孝建中，累遷豫州刺史，監五州諸軍事。

translations.literal: During the Xiaojian era he was promoted repeatedly to Inspector of Yuzhou and overseer of military affairs in five provinces.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaojian reign he rose step by step to Inspector of Yuzhou, supervising military affairs across five provinces.

sentences.zh: 先是，鄉人庾業，家甚富豪，方丈之膳，以待賓客，而慤至，設以菜葅粟飯，謂客曰：「宗軍人，慣噉粗食。」

translations.literal: Earlier, his fellow townsman Yu Ye was extremely wealthy. His meals for guests filled a square zhang, yet when Que came he set out pickled vegetables and millet rice and told the guests, "Commander Zong is a military man—he is used to coarse food."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, his townsman Yu Ye had been enormously rich, setting feasts that filled a square zhang for his guests. When Que visited, Ye served only pickles and millet gruel, telling the company, "Commander Zong is a soldier—he is accustomed to plain fare."

sentences.zh: 慤致飽而去。

translations.literal: Que ate his fill and left.
translations.idiomatic: Que ate his fill and departed.

sentences.zh: 至是業為慤長史，帶梁郡，慤待之甚厚，不以前事為嫌。

translations.literal: By then Ye was Que's chief administrator with concurrent command of Liang Commandery, and Que treated him very generously, taking no offense at the past.
translations.idiomatic: By then Ye served as Que's chief administrator with concurrent authority over Liang Commandery, and Que treated him with great kindness, bearing no grudge for the old slight.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，竟陵王誕據廣陵反，慤表求赴討，乘驛詣都，面受節度，上停輿慰勉，慤聳躍數十，左右顧盻，上壯之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming, the Prince of Jingling, Dan, held Guangling in revolt. Que memorialized asking to go to suppress him, rode post-horses to the capital, and received orders in person. The emperor halted his carriage to encourage him. Que leapt several tens of times, glancing left and right; the emperor was impressed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daming, the Prince of Jingling, Dan, rebelled at Guangling. Que petitioned to lead the suppression, raced by post relay to the capital, and received his commission face to face. The emperor stopped his carriage to exhort him. Que sprang up and down dozens of times, looking about him; the emperor was stirred.

sentences.zh: 及行，隸車騎大將軍沈慶之。

translations.literal: On the march he was placed under the Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he served under Shen Qingzhi, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 初，誕誑其眾云：「宗慤助我。」

translations.literal: At first Dan had deceived his troops, saying, "Zong Que is helping me."
translations.idiomatic: At first Dan had deceived his men, saying, "Zong Que is on my side."

sentences.zh: 及慤至，躍馬繞城呼曰：「我宗慤也。」

translations.literal: When Que arrived he spurred his horse around the walls and shouted, "I am Zong Que!"
translations.idiomatic: When Que arrived he galloped around the walls crying, "I am Zong Que!"

sentences.zh: 事平，入為左衞將軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he entered the capital as General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed he returned to court as General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 五年，從獵墮馬，脚折不堪朝直，以為光祿大夫，加金紫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, while hunting he fell from his horse and broke his leg, unable to attend court. He was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon added.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he fell from his horse while hunting, broke his leg, and could no longer attend court. He was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 慤有佳牛堪進御，官買不肯賣，坐免官。

translations.literal: Que had a fine ox fit to present to the throne. When the authorities wished to buy it he would not sell and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Que owned an excellent ox suitable for presentation to the throne. When officials sought to purchase it he refused to sell and was removed from his post.

sentences.zh: 明年，復職。

translations.literal: The next year he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was reappointed.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，為寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Que was made Colonel Pacifying the Tribes and Inspector of Yongzhou with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor acceded, Que was made Colonel Pacifying the Tribes and Inspector of Yongzhou with overall military authority.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征西將軍，諡曰肅侯。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West; his posthumous title was Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the West; his posthumous title was Marquis Su ("Solemn").

sentences.zh: 泰始二年，詔以慤配食孝武廟。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi an edict ordered that Que receive offerings in Emperor Xiaowu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi an edict granted him a place in the sacrifices at Emperor Xiaowu's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 子羅雲，卒，子元寶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Luoyun died; his grandson Yuanbao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luoyun died; the title passed to his grandson Yuanbao.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨

translations.literal: Wang Xuanmo
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo

sentences.zh: 王玄謨字彥德，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanmo, style name Yande, was a man of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo, whose courtesy name was Yande, came from Qi in Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖宏，河東太守，綿竹侯，以從叔司徒允之難，棄官北居新興，仍為新興、鴈門太守，其自敍云爾。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Hong was Administrator of Hedong and Marquis of Mianzhu. Because of the troubles of his cousin-by-marriage, Minister of Works Wang Yun, he abandoned office and went north to settle in Xinxing, then served as Administrator of Xinxing and Yanmen. He himself recorded this.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back, his ancestor Hong had been Administrator of Hedong and Marquis of Mianzhu. When his collateral paternal uncle, Minister over the Masses Wang Yun, met disaster, Hong resigned and moved north to Xinxing, later serving as administrator of Xinxing and Yanmen—so his own family record ran.

sentences.zh: 祖牢，仕慕容氏為上谷太守，陷慕容德，居青州。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lao served the Murong as Administrator of Shanggu, was captured by Murong De, and lived in Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lao had served the Murong as Administrator of Shanggu, fell into Murong De's hands, and settled in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父秀，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Xiu died young.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiu died early.

sentences.zh: 玄謨幼而不羣，世父蕤有知人鑒，常笑曰：「此兒氣概高亮，有太尉彥雲之風。」

translations.literal: Xuanmo was unruly from boyhood. His father's elder brother Rui had a gift for judging men and would often laugh, saying, "This boy's spirit is lofty and bright; he has the air of Grand Commandant Yan Yun."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo was wild even as a boy. His uncle Rui, who could read character well, would laugh and say, "The lad's bearing is high and bright—he has something of Grand Commandant Yan Yun about him."

sentences.zh: 武帝臨徐州，辟為從事史，與語異之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was in Xuzhou he summoned him as an attendant clerk and, speaking with him, found him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu held Xuzhou he summoned Xuanmo as an attendant clerk and, in conversation, found him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 少帝末，謝晦為荊州，請為南蠻行參軍、武寧太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Shaodi's reign, Xie Hui was in Jingzhou and invited him as Southern Tribes Acting Staff Officer and Defender of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Shaodi's reign, Xie Hui governed Jingzhou and took him on as acting staff officer for the southern tribes and as Defender of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 晦敗，以非大帥見原。

translations.literal: When Hui was defeated, because Xuanmo had not been a chief commander he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui fell, Xuanmo was spared because he had not been a principal commander.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，補長沙王義欣鎮軍中兵參軍，領汝陰太守。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he was made Central Army staff officer to the Prince of Changsha, Yixin, with concurrent office as Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanjia he was appointed staff officer in the central army of the Prince of Changsha, Yixin, while also serving as Administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 時虜攻陷滑臺，執朱脩之以歸。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarians attacked and took Huatai, carrying Zhu Xiuzhi away.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the enemy stormed Huatai and carried Zhu Xiuzhi off captive.

sentences.zh: 玄謨上疏曰：「王途始開，隨復淪塞，非惟天時，抑亦人事。

translations.literal: Xuanmo submitted a memorial saying, "The royal road has only just opened, yet it is again lost and blocked—this is not heaven's season alone but also human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo submitted a memorial: "The imperial highway has only just been reopened, yet it is blocked again—not by season alone, but by human failure.

sentences.zh: 虎牢、滑臺，豈惟將之不良，抑亦本之不固。

translations.literal: Hulao and Huatai—was it only that the generals were poor, or also that the foundations were not firm?
translations.idiomatic: For Hulao and Huatai, was the fault only in the generals, or also in weak foundations?

sentences.zh: 本之不固，皆由民憚遠役。

translations.literal: When the foundations are not firm, it is because the people dread distant corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Weak foundations come from the people's dread of distant service.

sentences.zh: 臣請以西陽之魯陽，襄陽之南鄉，發甲卒，分為兩道，直趣淆、澠，征士無遠徭之思，吏士有屢休之歌。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to mobilize armor-bearers from Luyang in Xiyang and Nanxiang in Xiangyang, divide them into two columns, and strike straight for Xiao and Mian, so that the drafted soldiers feel no thought of far-off service and officers and men have songs of repeated rest.
translations.idiomatic: I propose drafting soldiers from Luyang in Xiyang and Nanxiang in Xiangyang, splitting them into two columns to drive straight on Xiao and Mian, so conscripts need not fear distant levy and troops may enjoy real respite.

sentences.zh: 若欲以東國之眾，經營牢、洛，道途既遠，獨克實難。」

translations.literal: If you wish to use the masses of the eastern domains to operate on Hulao and Luoyang, the roads are long and success alone would be hard."
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to move the eastern provinces' manpower against Hulao and Luoyang, the distances are great and victory would be hard to win alone."

sentences.zh: 玄謨每陳北侵之策，上謂殷景仁曰：「聞王玄謨陳說，使人有封狼居胥意。」

translations.literal: Each time Xuanmo urged a northern campaign, the emperor told Yin Jingren, "When I hear Wang Xuanmo's proposals I feel the will to enfeoff Wolf Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Xuanmo pressed plans for northern invasion, the emperor told Yin Jingren, "Hearing Wang Xuanmo speak always stirs in me the ambition of enfeoffing Wolf Mountain."

sentences.zh: 後為興安侯義賓輔國司馬、彭城太守。

translations.literal: Later he was made Pacifying-State staff officer to the Marquis of Xing'an, Yibin, and Administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made staff officer to the Pacifying State for Marquis of Xing'an Yibin and Administrator of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 義賓薨，玄謨上表，以彭城要兼水陸，請以皇子撫臨州事，乃以孝武出鎮。

translations.literal: When Yibin died, Xuanmo submitted a memorial that Pengcheng was vital on land and water and asked that a prince oversee the province. Thereupon Emperor Xiaowu was sent to hold the post.
translations.idiomatic: After Yibin's death, Xuanmo memorialized that Pengcheng was crucial by land and water and asked that a prince govern the province; Emperor Xiaowu was then sent to take command.

sentences.zh: 及大舉北征，以玄謨為寧朔將軍，前鋒入河，受輔國將軍蕭斌節度。

translations.literal: When the great northern campaign was launched, Xuanmo was made General Who Pacifies the North, advanced as vanguard into the Yellow River, and placed under the command of Pacifying-State General Xiao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: When the great northern expedition was mounted, Xuanmo was made General Who Pacifies the North, led the vanguard across the Yellow River, and served under Pacifying-State General Xiao Bin.

sentences.zh: 玄謨向碻磝，戍主奔走，遂圍滑臺，積旬不克。

translations.literal: Xuanmo advanced on Queao; the garrison commander fled, and he besieged Huatai but could not take it in many days.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo pressed toward Queao; the defending commander fled, and he laid siege to Huatai, yet after many days still could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 虜主託跋燾率大眾號百萬，鞞鼓之聲，震動天地。

translations.literal: The barbarian ruler Tuoba Tao led a great host said to number a million; the sound of drums and flutes shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: The northern ruler Tuoba Tao marched with a host said to reach a million men; drum and horn rolled across the sky.

sentences.zh: 玄謨軍眾亦盛，器械甚精，而玄謨專依所見，多行殺戮。

translations.literal: Xuanmo's army was also large and his weapons very fine, yet Xuanmo relied solely on his own views and killed many.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo's force was likewise strong and his equipment excellent, but he trusted only his own judgment and put many to death.

sentences.zh: 初圍城，城內多茅屋，眾求以火箭燒之，玄謨恐損亡軍實，不從。

translations.literal: When the siege began the town held many thatched houses. The men asked to burn them with fire-arrows; Xuanmo feared loss to military stores and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: At first the city was full of thatched roofs. His men urged firing them with fire-arrows; Xuanmo refused, fearing damage to captured supplies.

sentences.zh: 城中即撤壞之，空地以為窟室。

translations.literal: The townsmen at once tore them down and cleared open ground for burrowed shelters.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders promptly stripped the thatch and cleared ground for dug-in shelters.

sentences.zh: 及魏救將至，眾請發車為營，又不從，將士多離怨。

translations.literal: When Wei relief was about to arrive, the troops asked to set up wagons as ramparts; again he refused, and many officers and men grew resentful and left.
translations.idiomatic: As Wei reinforcements approached, the army asked to ring the camp with wagons; again he refused, and officers and men drifted away in resentment.

sentences.zh: 又營貨利，一匹布責人八百梨，以此倍失人心。

translations.literal: He also traded for profit, charging eight hundred pears for one bolt of cloth, and thus doubled the loss of hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He also profiteered in camp goods, demanding eight hundred pears for a single bolt of cloth, and lost twice over in goodwill.

sentences.zh: 及託跋燾軍至，乃奔退，麾下散亡略盡。

translations.literal: When Tuoba Tao's army arrived, he fled in rout; his followers scattered almost to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuoba Tao's army came up, he broke and ran; his command dissolved almost entirely.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌將斬之，沈慶之固諫曰：「佛狸威震天下，控弦百萬，豈玄謨所能當。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin was about to execute him when Shen Qingzhi strongly remonstrated, saying, "Boli's might shakes the realm—he commands a million bowstrings. How could Xuanmo withstand him?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin was ready to behead him, but Shen Qingzhi pleaded hard: "Boli's power shakes the empire—he commands a million bowmen. Xuanmo could never have stood against him.

sentences.zh: 且殺戰將以自弱，非良計也。」

translations.literal: To kill a fighting general and thus weaken ourselves is no good plan."
translations.idiomatic: Slaying a field commander only weakens us—that is no wise course."

sentences.zh: 斌乃止。

translations.literal: Bin then stayed his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Bin stayed the execution.

sentences.zh: 初，玄謨始將見殺，夢人告曰：「誦觀音經千遍，則免。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xuanmo was first to be killed, a man told him in a dream, "Recite the Guanyin Sutra a thousand times and you will be spared."
translations.idiomatic: When he had first faced execution, a dream told him, "Chant the Guanyin Sutra a thousand times and you will escape death."

sentences.zh: 既覺，誦之得千遍，明日將刑，誦之不輟，忽傳呼停刑。

translations.literal: On waking he chanted until he reached a thousand. The next day, as execution was about to fall, he did not cease chanting. Suddenly came a call to halt the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He woke and chanted until he had completed a thousand verses. The next day, on the scaffold, he kept chanting without pause until an order suddenly halted the sentence.

sentences.zh: 遣代守碻磝，江夏王義恭為征討都督，以為碻磝不可守，召令還，為魏軍所追，大破之，流矢中臂。

translations.literal: He was sent to hold Queao in another's place. The Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, was overall commander for the punitive campaign. Judging Queao indefensible, he summoned Xuanmo back; the Wei army pursued and routed him badly, and a stray arrow struck his arm.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to hold Queao. Yigong, Prince of Jiangxia, commanded the punitive force, judged Queao untenable, and recalled him. Wei troops pursued and shattered his column; a stray arrow pierced his arm.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，還至歷城，義恭與玄謨書曰：「聞因敗為成，臂上金瘡，得非金印之徵也。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year he returned to Licheng. Yigong wrote to Xuanmo, "I hear that from defeat came success, and a golden wound on the arm—is this not the sign of a golden seal?"
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year he reached Licheng. Yigong wrote, "They say defeat turned to victory and a golden wound appeared on your arm—surely that foretells a golden seal?"

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，玄謨為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: When the deposed heir murdered his way to the throne, Xuanmo was made Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the heir Yuanxiong murdered his father and seized the throne, Xuanmo was appointed Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 孝武伐逆，玄謨遣濟南太守垣護之將兵赴義。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu marched against the usurper, Xuanmo sent the Administrator of Jinan, Yuan Huzhi, with troops to aid the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched to punish the usurper, Xuanmo sent Jinan Administrator Yuan Huzhi with troops to join the loyal side.

sentences.zh: 事平，除徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was made Inspector of Xuzhou with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: After the revolt was crushed he became Inspector of Xuzhou with overall military authority.

sentences.zh: 及南郡王義宣與江州刺史臧質反，朝庭假玄謨輔國將軍，拜豫州刺史，與柳元景南討，軍屯梁山，夾岸築偃月壘，水陸待之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nanjun, Yixuan, and the Inspector of Jiangzhou, Zang Zhi, rebelled, the court made Xuanmo acting Pacifying-State General and Inspector of Yuzhou, and with Liu Yuanying marched south to attack. The army encamped at Liangshan and built crescent ramparts along both banks to await them by land and water.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan, Prince of Nanjun, and Jiangzhou Inspector Zang Zhi rose in revolt, the court named Xuanmo acting Pacifying-State General and Inspector of Yuzhou. With Liu Yuanying he marched south, encamped at Liangshan, and threw up crescent ramparts on both riverbanks to meet the rebels by land and water.

sentences.zh: 義宣遣劉諶之就臧質，陳軍城南，玄謨留老弱守城，悉精兵接戰，賊遂大潰。

translations.literal: Yixuan sent Liu Shenzhi to join Zhi. They arrayed their army south of the city. Xuanmo left the old and weak to hold the town and led all his picked troops to battle; the rebels were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan sent Liu Shenzhi to Zang Zhi's camp. The rebels drew up south of the city. Xuanmo left the aged and weak to guard the walls and led every able man to the fight; the enemy collapsed.

sentences.zh: 加都督、前將軍，封曲江縣侯。

translations.literal: Overall command and the post of Forward General were added; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He received overall command and the rank of Forward General and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 中軍司馬劉沖之白孝武，言：「玄謨在梁山，與義宣通謀。」

translations.literal: Central Army staff officer Liu Chongzhi reported to Emperor Xiaowu, saying, "At Liangshan, Xuanmo was in secret league with Yixuan."
translations.idiomatic: Central Army staff officer Liu Chongzhi reported to Emperor Xiaowu, saying, "At Liangshan, Xuanmo was secretly colluding with Yixuan."

sentences.zh: 上意不能明，使有司奏玄謨多取寶貨，虛張戰簿，與徐州刺史垣護之並免官。

translations.literal: The emperor could not see clearly. He had the authorities memorialize that Xuanmo had taken many treasures and inflated battle rolls, and both he and Xuzhou Inspector Yuan Huzhi were removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not judge the charge clearly. He had officials report that Xuanmo had seized great spoils and falsified battle records; both he and Xuzhou Inspector Yuan Huzhi were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋復為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮上亡命司馬黑石推立夏侯方進為主，改姓李名弘，以惑眾，玄謨討斬之。

translations.literal: On the Huai a fugitive named Sima Heishi set up Xia Houfangjin as leader, changed his surname to Li and his name to Hong, to delude the masses; Xuanmo attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: A Huai River outlaw, Sima Heishi, proclaimed Xia Houfangjin leader, styled him Li Hong to beguile the people; Xuanmo crushed the band and executed him.

sentences.zh: 遷寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Colonel Pacifying the Tribes and Inspector of Yongzhou with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Colonel Pacifying the Tribes and Inspector of Yongzhou with overall authority.

sentences.zh: 雍土多僑寓，玄謨請土斷流民，當時百姓不願屬籍，罷之。

translations.literal: Yong had many sojourners; Xuanmo asked to fix native registers for the floating population. The people then did not wish to be entered on the rolls, and the measure was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou held many displaced households. Xuanmo petitioned to register wandering populations locally; the people resisted enrollment and the policy was dropped.

sentences.zh: 其年，玄謨又令九品以上租，使貧富相通，境內莫不嗟怨。

translations.literal: That year Xuanmo also ordered rent from men of the ninth rank and above, forcing rich and poor to share the burden; throughout the commandery none did not sigh in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he levied rent even on men of the ninth rank and above, forcing rich and poor to share alike; the whole province groaned in protest.

sentences.zh: 民間訛言玄謨欲反，時柳元景當權，元景弟僧景為新城太守，以元景之勢，制令南陽、順陽、上庸、新城諸郡並發兵討玄謨。

translations.literal: Rumors spread that Xuanmo would rebel. Liu Yuanying then held power; Yuanying's younger brother Sengjing was Administrator of Xincheng and, relying on Yuanying's influence, ordered Nanyang, Shunyang, Shangyong, Xincheng, and other commanderies all to raise troops against Xuanmo.
translations.idiomatic: Word ran that Xuanmo meant to rebel. Liu Yuanying then dominated the court; his brother Sengjing governed Xincheng and, leaning on Yuanying's power, ordered Nanyang, Shunyang, Shangyong, Xincheng, and neighboring commanderies to march against Xuanmo.

sentences.zh: 玄謨令內外晏然，以解眾惑，馳啟孝武，具陳本末。

translations.literal: Xuanmo ordered inner and outer calm to dispel the people's doubts and sent a swift report to Emperor Xiaowu, setting out the whole story.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo kept his household and camp unruffled to quiet rumor and rushed a full account to Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 帝知其虛，馳遣主書吳喜公撫慰之，又答曰：「梁山風塵，初不介意，君臣之際，過足相保，聊復為笑，伸卿眉頭。」

translations.literal: The emperor knew the charge was false and sent Chief Clerk Wu Xigong posthaste to comfort him, replying also, "The dust of Liangshan—I never minded it. Between lord and minister we have more than enough to trust one another. Let us laugh again and unknit your brow."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the accusation hollow, the emperor dispatched Chief Clerk Wu Xigong to reassure him and wrote back, "The turmoil at Liangshan never troubled me. Between sovereign and minister we have more than enough trust—come, let us laugh again and smooth your brow."

sentences.zh: 玄謨性嚴，未嘗妄笑，時人言玄謨眉頭未曾伸，故帝以此戲之。

translations.literal: Xuanmo was stern by nature and never laughed lightly. Men of the time said his brow had never unknit; hence the emperor jested thus.
translations.idiomatic: Stern by nature, he seldom smiled; people said his brow had never relaxed—hence the emperor's jest.

sentences.zh: 後為金紫光祿大夫，領太常。

translations.literal: Later he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon, and headed the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple ribbon, while also heading the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 及建明堂，以本官領起部尚書，又領北選。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was built, he retained his title and also headed the Ministry for Hall Construction and northern selection of officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall was raised, he kept his rank, headed the ministry overseeing its construction, and supervised northern appointments.

sentences.zh: 孝武狎侮羣臣，隨其狀貌，各有比類，多鬚者謂之羊。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu treated his ministers familiarly and insultingly, matching each to his looks with a nickname: the bearded he called "goat."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu bullied his ministers and mocked their faces with nicknames—men with heavy beards he called "goats."

sentences.zh: 顏師伯缺齒，號之曰齴。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo lacked teeth; he was dubbed "gummy."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo was missing teeth; they nicknamed him "Gummy."

sentences.zh: 劉秀之儉吝，呼為老慳。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuzhi was miserly; they called him "old skinflint."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuzhi was tight-fisted; they called him "Old Miser."

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎宗靈秀體肥，拜起不便，每至集會，多所賜與，欲其瞻謝傾踣，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zong Lingxiu was corpulent and awkward in bowing and rising. At every gathering the emperor gave him many gifts, wishing that when he looked up to give thanks he would stumble and fall for laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Zong Lingxiu was obese and clumsy at court bows. At every feast the emperor showered him with gifts, hoping he would trip when he rose to thank him and provide a laugh.

sentences.zh: 又刻木作靈秀父光祿勳叔獻像，送其家廳事。

translations.literal: He also carved a wooden image of Lingxiu's father, the Superintendent of the Imperial Household Shuxian, and sent it to their family hall.
translations.idiomatic: He even had a wooden statue carved of Lingxiu's father, Superintendent of the Imperial Household Shuxian, and sent it to their reception hall.

sentences.zh: 柳元景、垣護之並北人，而玄謨獨受「老傖」之目。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanying and Yuan Huzhi were both northerners, yet Xuanmo alone bore the label "old barbarian."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanying and Yuan Huzhi were northerners too, yet only Xuanmo was tagged "Old Barbarian."

sentences.zh: 凡所稱謂，四方書疏亦如之。

translations.literal: Whatever names he gave, letters from the four directions used them likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever nicknames he coined, correspondence from every quarter repeated them.

sentences.zh: 嘗為玄謨作四時詩曰：「菫荼供春膳，粟漿充夏飡。

translations.literal: He once composed a four-season poem for Xuanmo, saying, "Shepherd's purse supplies the spring meal; millet gruel fills the summer board.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote Xuanmo a poem on the four seasons: "Shepherd's purse for spring fare; millet broth for summer meals.

sentences.zh: 瓟醬調秋菜，白醝解冬寒。」

translations.literal: Gourd sauce seasons autumn greens; white lees break winter's cold."
translations.idiomatic: Gourd paste dresses autumn greens; rice wine lees ward off winter chill."

sentences.zh: 又寵一崐崘奴子，名白主。

translations.literal: He also favored a Kunlun slave boy named Baizhu.
translations.idiomatic: He also doted on a Kunlun slave boy named Baizhu ("White Master").

sentences.zh: 常在左右，令以杖擊羣臣，自柳元景以下，皆罹其毒。

translations.literal: He kept him always at his side and ordered him to strike the ministers with a staff; from Liu Yuanying down, all suffered at his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Baizhu stayed always at his side, and the emperor had him beat the ministers with a staff—from Liu Yuanying downward, all felt his blows.

sentences.zh: 玄謨尋遷平北將軍、徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Xuanmo was soon transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo was soon made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xuzhou with overall authority.

sentences.zh: 時北土飢饉，乃散私穀十萬斛、牛千頭以振之。

translations.literal: The north was then in famine; he distributed 100,000 hu of his private grain and a thousand head of cattle to relieve the distress.
translations.idiomatic: Famine gripped the north; he released 100,000 hu of his private grain and a thousand oxen for relief.

sentences.zh: 轉領軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，與柳元景等俱受顧命，以外監事委玄謨。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, he and Liu Yuanying and others alike received the dying charge; foreign affairs were entrusted to Xuanmo.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaowu's death he and Liu Yuanying and others received the final testament; border affairs were placed in Xuanmo's hands.

sentences.zh: 時朝政多門，玄謨以嚴直不容，徙青、冀二州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Government then had many factions; Xuanmo's stern uprightness could not be tolerated, and he was moved to Inspector of Qing and Ji with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Court factions multiplied; Xuanmo's stern integrity could not be borne, and he was shifted to Inspector of Qing and Ji with overall command.

sentences.zh: 少帝既誅顏師伯、柳元景等，狂悖益甚，以領軍徵玄謨。

translations.literal: After the Deposed Emperor had executed Yan Shibo, Liu Yuanying, and others, his frenzy grew worse. He summoned Xuanmo as General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the Deposed Emperor killed Yan Shibo, Liu Yuanying, and the rest, his madness deepened. He recalled Xuanmo as General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 子姪咸勸稱疾，玄謨曰：「吾受先帝厚恩，豈可畏禍苟免。」

translations.literal: His sons and nephews all urged him to plead illness. Xuanmo said, "I received deep grace from the late emperor—how could I fear disaster and seek an easy escape?"
translations.idiomatic: Sons and nephews begged him to feign sickness. Xuanmo said, "The late emperor favored me deeply—how could I shrink from peril and save myself?"

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: He set out.
translations.idiomatic: He went.

sentences.zh: 及至，屢表諫諍，又流涕請緩刑去殺，以安元元。

translations.literal: When he arrived he memorialized repeatedly in remonstrance and, weeping, begged that punishments be eased and killings stopped to settle the common people.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching court he remonstrated again and again, weeping as he begged that executions be slowed and slaughter ended so the people might be calmed.

sentences.zh: 少帝大怒。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，禮遇甚優。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xuanmo was treated with great honor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming succeeded, Xuanmo was honored generously.

sentences.zh: 時四方反叛，以玄謨為大統，領水軍南討，以脚疾，聽乘輿出入。

translations.literal: Rebellions rose on every side; he was made supreme commander, led the navy south to suppress them, and because of his leg ailment was permitted to enter and leave by imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: With revolt breaking out everywhere, he was named supreme commander and led the fleet south; his leg trouble won him leave to ride the imperial carriage in and out of court.

sentences.zh: 尋除車騎將軍、江州刺史，副司徒建安王於赭圻，賜以諸葛亮筩袖鎧。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Jiangzhou, second to the Minister of Works, the Prince of Jian'an, at Zheqi, and was given Zhuge Liang's tube-and-sleeve armor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Jiangzhou, serving under the Minister of Works, Prince of Jian'an, at Zheqi, and was presented with Zhuge Liang's linked tube armor.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，領護軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the ceremony of the Three Excellencies, and headed the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he became Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the honors of the Three Excellencies and commanded the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 遷南豫州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He was moved to Inspector of Southern Yuzhou with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Southern Yuzhou with overall military authority.

sentences.zh: 玄謨性嚴剋少恩，而將軍宗越御下更苛酷，軍士謂之語曰：「寧作五年徒，不逢王玄謨。

translations.literal: Xuanmo was stern and sparing of kindness; the general Zong Yue was yet harsher with his men. The soldiers had a saying: "Better five years as a convict than meet Wang Xuanmo.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo was harsh and stinting in mercy; General Zong Yue was crueller still. The troops had a rhyme: "Better five years as a convict than run into Wang Xuanmo.

sentences.zh: 玄謨猶自可，宗越更殺我。」

translations.literal: Xuanmo is still bearable; Yue will kill you."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo you can endure—Yue will kill you."

sentences.zh: 年八十一薨，諡曰莊公。

translations.literal: At eighty-one he died; his posthumous title was Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one; his posthumous title was Duke Zhuang ("Solemn").

sentences.zh: 子深早卒，深子繢嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shen died young; Shen's son Hui inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen died early; the line passed to Shen's son Hui.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historian's appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：脩之、宗慤，皆以將帥之材，懷廉潔之操，有足稱焉。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xiuzhi and Zong Que both had the talent of generals and bore integrity in frugality—there is reason to praise them.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Both Xiuzhi and Zong Que possessed true generalship and maintained frugal integrity—each merits praise.

sentences.zh: 玄謨雖苛剋少恩，然觀其大節，亦足為美。

translations.literal: Though Xuanmo was harsh and sparing of kindness, viewed in his great principles he is also worthy of esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo, for all his harshness and scant mercy, shows in his larger conduct something still admirable.

sentences.zh: 當少帝失道，多所殺戮，而能冒履不測，傾心輔弼，斯可謂忘身徇國者歟。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor lost the Way and killed many, Xuanmo could still brave the unknown and give his heart to aid the throne—may this not be called forgetting self and serving the state?
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor abandoned the Way and slaughtered without measure, Xuanmo still risked the unknown and gave his heart to steady the throne—can this be anything but forgetting self for the sake of the realm?
